_comment: The map database of D33: reveal tuning and every landmark the map may ever show. Data-driven so Band 1-4 landmarks (quarry, warrens, river, mill, relay) join by editing this file, not code. Tunable.
_comment_reveal_radius_ow3: OW3 raised this 45 -> 80. TUNABLE. With fog fully opaque again (tab_map.gd/minimap.gd), 45m revealed a ribbon barely wider than the road, which is what made an honest fog read as "nothing but black" the last time it was opaque. Widening the reveal is the lever that keeps the fog truthful without the map being a void; darkening or lightening the fog itself is the lever that has now been swung three times.
_comment_starting_reveal: ralph/OWNER_DIRECTIVES_2026-08-22.md section 3: 'The village and the roads out of it start revealed... The player does not start blind in their own home town.' map_state.gd::_seed_starting_reveal already existed and reads this array; it was only ever empty, so a fresh save opened a black rectangle (OP21-15). Each entry is a fog circle seeded before the player takes a step, sited on the SAME `paths.routes` polylines terrain_playground.json authors the village's four dirt roads from (Grandpa's House, Practice Meadow, The Pond, The Rise) -- so a road move carries this reveal with it rather than stranding it. One circle at the square plus two per route (a midpoint and the route's own end) covers the road corridor without reaching past it; `discovered_fraction` on the current 2048x8192m world comes out under 0.2%, nowhere near spec sec16's 'does not reveal everything automatically' line. TUNABLE.
_comment_starting_reveal_op23_03: OP23-03 (owner playtest 2026-08-23): the reveal above passed test_map_fog's '>0%' floor at ~0.12% of the world and still read as 'the map is still a black rectangle' -- correct on a fresh-save full-map view, where these circles are specks against a 2048x8192m corridor, and the fix the 2026-08-22 ruling above already asked for (VISIBLY revealed village + roads) needed a bigger lever than the floor test alone caught. Tripled every radius (village 50->150, each 20->60, each 25->75): the raw sum-of-circles area goes from ~20,028m^2 to ~180,252m^2, but these circles overlap along each road, so the actual measured `discovered_fraction` lands at ~0.6% -- still a real ~5x jump over the old ~0.12% seed, reading as one connected revealed corridor around the village rather than nine faint dots, while staying comfortably under the 5% ceiling test_map_fog also enforces (spec sec16: 'does not reveal everything automatically'). TUNABLE.

starting_reveal._why: Grandpa's House road, end (also covers the grandpa_house landmark)
The Rise road, midpoint (also road_gate approach)
The Rise road, walkable end (OF10a's truncation point)

landmarks._comment_ow5d: Historical: OW5D temporarily pinned this at the table's explicit stronghold coordinate (0,7560), a simplification since the castle silhouette (`landmark.gd`) and the walkable route (`stronghold.json`) were then two unrelated buildings. GATE-E2 then pointed it at the castle's own re-derived `SITE` instead. Both are superseded below.
landmarks._comment_gate_e2: Historical: GATE-E2 (2026-08-23) pointed this pin at `landmark.gd`'s then-detached castle SITE (150,7595), 154m from the stronghold's own route -- correct for a world with two buildings, superseded now that there is one.
landmarks._comment_t1_hall: T1-HALL (2026-08-30): the castle and the stronghold are one location (`HALL_DESIGN_2026-08-30.md`); `landmark.gd`'s silhouette at (150,7595) retires and nothing stands there any more. This pin now marks the merged complex's own centre of mass -- `stronghold.json`'s `site.at` (8,7560) offset toward the courtyard/keep half of the built footprint, not the outer works' own centre -- so the map marker sits over the middle of the actual building rather than its front gate. `silhouette: true` is kept: this is still a landmark seen from across the meadow before it is reached, exactly the role it played for the castle pin.

landmarks._comment_ow5d: OW5D: south_bridge crossing itself moved to (0,1330) (docs/MEADOWS_MACRO_LAYOUT.md section 10.2), translated by the same (-5,+1250) this landmark follows.

OW5D relocation: this file's own comment below says 'Position is the site centre data/config/relay_site.json authored ... if it moves, all three move together' -- moved to match relay_site.json's new `site.centre` (350,3760).

OW5D, docs/MEADOWS_MACRO_LAYOUT.md section 10.2: the crossing's own terrain_playground.json entries (`crossings[1]`, `flats[9,10]`, the river) are OW5C's job and were left untouched by this pass, but the task explicitly asked this landmark to be relocated anyway, to (-150,4200), so the map does not show the crossing at its old empty coordinates in the meantime.
landmarks._comment_ow5c_seam: OW5C follow-up: matches the crossing itself after its -2m seam-workaround shift (-150 -> -152).

landmarks._comment_d1: BAND1-D1. The pond-to-bridge corridor's rest stop (props.json's `trail_camp` cluster, vegetation.json clearing order 1000), at the spine's own (360,910) bend -- roughly the corridor's midpoint. `minor`/practical, not a `silhouette`: this is a waypoint to be found by walking to it and remembered, not a landmark seen from across the meadow, the same distinction old_mill_crossing's own comment draws.

landmarks._comment_band2_63: BAND2-63. The `camp` icon (assets/ui/icons/map/camp.png) has existed since the icon set shipped and no landmark has ever used it. This band's `ranger_camp` prop cluster and its matching `vegetation.json` clearing (both order 2001 in their files) are the region's one field-camp candidate (prompt 61's camp-siting brief); a `minor` pin here is the only way the map tells a player looking for a rest stop where it is, the same way `old_mill_crossing` and `tether_relay` already tell them where the chapter's other named stops are.

_comment_tether_relay: SE23, spec 3 Band 3. A `major` landmark: the chapter's first mini-stronghold and the rung of 32's ladder where Team Tether becomes a place rather than a rumour, not a piece of furniture on the way somewhere else. NOT a `silhouette` -- the stronghold is drawn before discovery because it is meant to be seen from across the meadow and never reached; the relay is meant to be walked into, so it appears the ordinary way, by going there. `relay` is an icon that already exists in assets/ui/icons/map/ and was drawn for exactly this. Position is the site centre data/config/relay_site.json authored and scripts/world/tether_relay.gd builds from -- if it moves, all three move together.
_comment_south_bridge: SC14, spec 3 Gate 1. A `major` landmark rather than a `minor` one: it is the chapter's first physical gate and the thing the whole south road exists to reach, not a piece of furniture on the way somewhere else. NOT a `silhouette` -- the stronghold is drawn before discovery because it is meant to be seen from across the meadow and never reached; the bridge is meant to be walked to on day one, so it appears the ordinary way, by going there. Position is the gully carve's own centre (terrain_playground.json `crossings[0].carve.centre`); if that moves, this moves.
_comment_regions: Owner directive, playtest pass: 'name some of the areas and uncover them like fortnite maps do.' A region is broader than a landmark -- the AREA around a point of interest, not the point itself -- and is discovered by entering it (map_state.gd::update_region), not by proximity like a landmark. A region is NOT one destination: a real Fortnite map names a handful of large, well-separated zones, not one per building. The first cut of this named village square, Grandpa's house and the practice meadow as three separate regions -- all real destinations (data/config/terrain_playground.json's own paths.routes[].label) but only 15-35m apart, so their labels landed on top of each other on the full map and read as clutter rather than geography. They are now one region, matching what they actually are: the single starting hub the player spends their first minutes in. The Pond and The Rise stay separate -- 150m+ from the hub and 230m from each other, genuinely distinct places a player walks TO, not three names for one dooryard. TUNABLE.

regions._comment_ow5d: OW5D relocation: same offset as `water.pond_centre` in terrain_playground.json, (-145,138)->(-395,545) -- this region's centre keeps its old (+53,-38) offset from the pond centre applied to the new one.
OW5D relocation, same uniform (+377,+1642) offset as the quarry itself (old anchor (23,158) -> new (400,1800)).
OW5D relocation, same (+242,+3726) offset as relay_site.json's `site.centre`.

regions._comment_mq2b: MQ2B, spec Sec3 Band 2. The chapter's required dungeon had a `site.at` in burrow_warrens.json and no map entry anywhere -- the Old Quarry (evidence, optional) had a named region and the required dungeon next to it did not. Centre is the site's own entrance point, the one part of the complex that is actually above ground and approachable; the chambers run in from there rather than around it, so naming the mouth names the place. Separation is comfortable and was checked: ~1065m to The Old Quarry, ~1498m to The Tether Relay, both bands away -- no overlap possible at this range. TUNABLE.
regions._comment_s06_leg_resite: GATE-F-LEG-S06. `centre` was still (-420,2470) -- the pre-BAND2-63-WARRENS site, before the cave was relocated to burrow_warrens.json's current `site.at` (-357,2610) because the old site could not be walked through (see that file's own `_comment_resiting`). BAND2_WARRENS_EVIDENCE_2026-08-23.md's file footprint claims this entry moved with the site; it did not take, or was reverted -- this SHA still had the 150m-stale value. A player using the Map tab to find the Warrens was pointed 150m from the real mouth, into unvetted terrain the site relocation never had to prove walkable (only the road-side approach from the spine was measured). An isolated S06 playtest, walking the map's own pin the way a player would, drove the player into that unvetted stretch and it went permanently unrecoverable there (`player_controller.gd`'s own entombment failsafe correctly declines to act -- the body is pressed against something with a clear alternate direction, not sealed -- so nothing ever moved it again). Moved to match `burrow_warrens.json`'s actual `site.at`; radius unchanged.

regions._comment_ow5d: OW5D, docs/MEADOWS_MACRO_LAYOUT.md section 10.2: the task explicitly asked BOTH `old_mill_crossing` and `the_long_water` to reference (-150,4200) -- the river/crossing geometry itself is OW5C's job and was not touched. This region's old centre (150,70) sat downstream of the old crossing on the river's own course; re-deriving an equivalent downstream offset on the NEW river course is OW5C's job too, so this was pinned to the same explicit reference point rather than guessed at.

regions._why: GATE-D4/prompt 65. Band 4 had zero named regions -- the whole 2240m had nothing on the map past The Long Water. This is the old-growth pocket on the western swing (bands/band4_upper_meadows_ironwood's own harvest.json order 4000-4004, spawns.json order 4000/4007/4008): the region's whole material tier, its one special encounter, and a night-ecology pocket, all one place rather than three unrelated pins. Landform name, no icon, same pattern as `the_rise`/`the_pond` above -- a discovered AREA, not a built structure with a pin. Centre sits between the grove's own harvest cluster and the trailpup/tuskroot/duskhush spawns it shares ground with; 60m carries all of them. Separation checked: 881m from The Long Water, comfortably clear.

GATE-D4/prompt 65. The watchtower spur: captain_ridge, the new optional patrol trainer and its camp dressing (trainers.json order 4000, props.json order 4000), and the resident galecrest (spawns.json order 4010) -- the 'ruined watch/occupation traces' and 'Team Tether patrol camps' spec Band 4 names as regional identity, given a name on the map the same way The Tether Relay was in Band 3. Landform-plus-occupation name, no icon, same pattern as the region entries above it. Centre sits between captain_ridge (-280,6460) and the patrol site (-235,6470); 55m carries both without reaching the high pasture loop's own Meadowhart herd 230m south. Separation checked: 1433m from The Ironwood Grove.

T3-BAND4. ralph/reports/finding-post-tournament-cadence-2026-08-29.md's second-worst authored-content gap (852m) sits between Captain Vess and the Stronghold Approach, where the route runs empty. `watchtower_landmark.gd` builds the actual ruin there (WATCHTOWER_AT in playground_world.gd); this names it on the map, same pattern as `the_ridgeline_watch` above -- a single built structure, not a broad area, so the radius stays tight rather than matching a region's usual 45-62m. No icon, matching every other landform/ruin entry in this list; a dedicated map icon is presentation work for the visual lane, not this pin's job. Separation checked: 424m from The Ridgeline Watch (band 4's other named ruin), comfortably clear -- these are the region's 'occupation traces' spec §3 names as recurring, not one feature repeated.

regions._comment:
T5-CADENCE, and D36's rule the same way The Long Water and The Tether Relay apply it: few and LARGE, one name for a whole stretch of country rather than one per feature. This is band 3's opening -- the ground where Stone & Root's uplands drain north and the water first gathers, from the band seam at (0,3180) to the bend onto the relay road. T4-REGIONS scored this stretch's route hierarchy PARTIAL with the reason in plain numbers: 'the band's first 668m and last 519m have no landmark at all', and criterion 12 FAIL at 668m of structurally empty spine. Three authored sites now stand in it -- the haulage wreck, the Lockwater Overlook and the Springhead (band3 props.json orders 3005-3007) -- and this is the name of the country they are in. The name is earned by the Springhead rather than invented over it: stone country whose water starts here.

SEPARATION, checked and not assumed, because that is the mistake this file's own `_comment_regions` records: 492m to The Tether Relay, 780m to The Long Water, 996m to The Burrow Warrens. No two labels can crowd. 70m carries all three sites; discovery is by ENTERING (map_state.gd::update_region), which for this region means crossing out of Stone & Root, which is the moment the audit says nothing currently acknowledges. TUNABLE.

T5-CADENCE. The eastern sweep of band 4, the 1161m T4-REGIONS measured as the longest structurally empty stretch in the game and named as the place a player who quits the Meadows will quit it. Three of this lane's four new band-4 sites sit inside it (the stock camp, the herd bull and the severed conduit post), and the audit's route-hierarchy finding is what this row answers: band 4's three existing regions 'cluster at the band's two ends ... The 1161m between has no landmark.'

THE NAME is the chapter's own, not new world-building: data/items/items.json's `field_sigil` calls the Field Captain's posting 'the high pasture posting', `pasture_drover_juno` works this road, and the herd this region is authored around is the band's 30 meadowhart. The high summer pasture, named.

SEPARATION, checked: 902m to The Ridgeline Watch, 968m to The Broken Tower, 1160m to The Ironwood Grove -- the most comfortable clearance of any region on this map, because the whole finding is that nothing is here. 65m carries the stock camp's own site and the herd ground; discovery is by ENTERING. TUNABLE.

_comment_the_tether_relay: SE23, and D36's rule applied the same way the quarry applies it: few and LARGE. ONE region for the whole station -- the approach road, the compound, the pad and the three conduit runs converging on it -- not one per feature. Its centre sits between the compound centre ([108,34]) and the apparatus pad ([104.5,23.1]) so the map label lands over the site rather than off one edge of it, and 48m carries the outermost pylon on every run. Separation: 111m to Grandpa's Village and 145m to The Old Quarry, both clear of any overlap. The Rise is the exception and the first authored overlap on this map -- 75m between centres against 55+48m of radius, so their rims cross in a 28m band. That is deliberate rather than sloppy: shrinking this region enough to avoid it entirely (20m) would stop it covering its own compound. map_state.gd::_region_at already defines the answer -- the nearest centre among every region you are inside wins -- so the band resolves on the midline and neither label moves. The two LABELS are 75m apart, which is the thing the first regions cut got wrong (three names 15-35m apart, printed on top of each other). Discovery is by ENTERING it (map_state.gd::update_region), which for this region means having gone past the quarry on the stronghold bearing. TUNABLE.
_comment_the_old_quarry: SD16, and D36's rule applied rather than quoted: few and LARGE. This is one region for the whole worked site -- the quarry floor, its foundations, the standing dead, and the conduit run leaving it on the stronghold bearing -- not one per feature, exactly the mistake D36 was written to correct. Its centre sits between the floor ([23,158]) and the first pylon out ([31.7,148.4]) so the map label lands over the site rather than off one edge of it, and 62m carries the whole run out to [41,121]. Separation from every existing region is comfortable: 175m to Grandpa's Village, 130m to The Pond, 205m to The Rise -- no two labels can crowd each other the way the first regions cut did. Discovery is by ENTERING it (map_state.gd::update_region), which for this region means having crossed the South Bridge, so the name arrives at the moment the gate pays off. TUNABLE.
_comment_old_mill_crossing: SE22, spec 3 Band 3's main gate, and `major` for the reason the South Bridge is: it is the only ground link across SE21's river, so it is the thing a whole band of the chapter exists to reach, not furniture on the way somewhere else. Shares the South Bridge's `bridge` icon deliberately -- the player has already learned what that mark means and what standing at one costs. Position is the river's narrows, terrain_playground.json crossings[1].channel.centre; if that moves, this moves.
_comment_the_long_water: SE21, and D36's rule again: few and LARGE. ONE region for the whole river -- both banks, the narrows, the mill, and the ground the water is the edge of -- not one for the crossing and another for the reach above it. Centre sits on the course itself just downstream of the Old Mill Crossing so the label lands over the water rather than off one bank, and 72m carries it up the reach to the gorge and down past the far bank the player first stands on. Separation is comfortable and was checked, not assumed: 129m to The Rise, 149m to The Old Quarry, 168m to Grandpa's Village -- no two labels can crowd each other. Discovery is by ENTERING (map_state.gd::update_region), which for this region means walking out to the water, and that is the point: the river is meant to be found by seeing it. The NAME is the one piece of world-building invented here rather than quoted from the spec (which says only 'a substantial river'); it is TUNABLE like everything else in this file and reads in the family the other three already set. MERGE NOTE (orchestrator): shipped at 72m and cut to 52m when SE21 and SE23 landed together — at 72m this region swallowed The Tether Relay's centre 59.5m away, and map_state's nearest-centre rule then depended on this file's order. 52m still carries the narrows, the Old Mill Crossing (30.5m out, the binding constraint) and the reach above it, and leaves 7.5m of clearance to the relay's centre. TUNABLE, but not upward past 59m without moving the relay.
